newsitem.title: USA: Canada spot butane prices up, propane steady.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot butane prices up, propane steady.

text.p: Spot prices of Canada butane were higher this week and propane held its value as cold weather in the eastern hub supported the liquefied petroleum gas, players said Thursday.
In the eastern hub of Sarnia, normal butane was up about a half cent this week to between 35.00 cents and 35.50 cents, in line with stronger U.S. values.
Isobutane also gained strength amid tight supply at around 44.00 cents.
According to government stock data, isobutane stocks were down by about 38 percent in April.

Edmonton field butane in western Canada rose by about 2.00 cents to 30.00 cents a gallon. A trader said 50,000 barrels of the material will begin to be shipped by the end of May into the Cochin pipeline to the Midwest.
Below-normal temperatures in Sarnia kept a floor under spot propane, which held at 37.50/38.50 cents, traders said.
"This cold weather is great business-wise. We are selling barrels we didn't sell off in January and February," said a Sarnia player.

According to the inventory data, propane stocks in the hub were up 36 percent, while stocks in the west were up about 30 percent. Total stocks were up 68 percent in the month but still 55 percent below year-ago levels. - ((Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1632))
